argumentMap.attributedThesis: AIDB argues that Astra is better understood as an opportunity model that enables unfamiliar work than as an efficiency model that merely improves familiar work.
reasoningChain: Early benchmark and practitioner results conflict because most established tests emphasize older task patterns.
Astra's most visible differences are computer use, 3D creation and longer connected work across software.
Those capabilities may change both what non-specialists can make and how people interact with computers.
The useful near-term job is testing concrete new workflows, not declaring a universal model winner.
argumentMap.editorialBoundary: This is AIDB's attributed analysis. Vendor benchmarks, social demonstrations, costs and practitioner results are not independent general-performance evidence.

items.heading: Delayed by design
items.reason: The launch delay is already covered; preserve only verified safety context.

items.heading: Cybersecurity partners got Astra first
items.reason: Exact phased-access and banked-reset conditions require current official evidence.

items.heading: The launch video shows hands-free work
items.reason: A vendor demonstration is useful direction-setting, not proof of routine capability.

items.heading: Every's mixed Astra review
items.reason: Distinct practitioner evidence of strong computer use and overcomplication, with attribution and task limits.

items.heading: Astra initially scored 61
items.reason: The benchmark version, weighting and current score need exact primary recovery.

items.heading: Artificial Analysis changed its index
items.reason: Potential evidence that old tests miss agentic work, but the exact methodology must be read.

items.heading: Opportunity model, not efficiency model
items.reason: Strong explanatory distinction; it is AIDB's thesis and should not overwrite the existing Daily.

items.heading: Coding performance and cost
items.reason: Benchmark identities, settings and cost calculations require originals.

items.heading: Maximum effort may overthink
items.reason: Potentially useful current practice, but only after task-specific independent testing.

items.heading: Computer use is the launch emphasis
items.reason: The current Daily already explains cross-application work and permissions.

items.heading: Science and math benchmarks
items.reason: High-stakes capability claims require benchmark and expert context.

items.heading: Exploit-building benchmark
items.reason: The current story already records the Critical cyber threshold; do not add unsupported inference.

items.heading: Blender demonstrations
items.reason: Promising examples, not evidence of reliable professional 3D work.

items.heading: One-shot games by non-engineers
items.reason: Useful illustration of access expansion once original examples and limitations are verified.

items.heading: Game cost and quota anecdotes
items.reason: Anecdotal account-specific cost cannot support general guidance.

items.heading: 3D as explanation
items.reason: Distinct teaching opportunity, but medical examples must not be treated as reliable health guidance.

items.heading: Visual work wins attention
items.reason: Ethan Mollick's attributed observation, not a performance conclusion.

items.heading: Coding may have saturated
items.reason: Mixed practitioner results prevent a universal-winner story and improve the viewpoint audit.

items.heading: One-shot product intelligence app
items.reason: One practitioner's result is useful only with exact workflow and failure conditions.

items.heading: Hands-off computer use
items.reason: A bounded workflow-inventory exercise may be useful; privacy and approval boundaries must be added.

items.heading: 3D as the third capability jump
items.reason: A durable question about capability access; it remains a hypothesis about adoption.

items.heading: Interaction pattern can matter more than capability
items.reason: Connects selective image editing, loops and computer use without reducing the lesson to longer prompts.

items.heading: Jarvis-style interaction may go mainstream
items.reason: Vendor direction and AIDB inference, not established mainstream behaviour.

items.heading: OpenAI says internal plans moved six months
items.reason: Interested-party internal claim with no independent causal evidence.

audienceGap.readerQuestion: Is Astra useful because it writes a better answer, or because it can carry a larger job through several tools?
audienceGap.plainLanguageRule: Start with a familiar multi-step assignment, show what the model can reach and do, then explain permissions, evidence and where a person still decides.

bigPictureThemeReview.reason: The opportunity-versus-efficiency distinction materially extends the existing capability-and-work theme, but does not authorize a Big Picture draft or publication.

internalPracticeReview.reason: Test Astra on one real cross-application workflow against Sol with the same acceptance criteria; do not adopt social demonstrations as operating proof.
